rationale: PINS GO40: a package-scope var/const whose declared type CONTAINS the type reference, reached without a func_literal in between. `resolveSource`'s func_literal branch reached a var_spec only by climbing THROUGH a function literal (`var R = map[string]func(){ ... }`), so a var whose declared type is a function type had no branch at all: its func type's parameter declarations walk parameter_list -> function_type -> var_spec and the walk continued straight past the var_spec to `global`. MEASURED DEFECT, proven before the fix on this exact declaration: FOUR `references` rows where the language has TWO facts. The var_spec pass published the correct `sysStat -> FileInfo @19` and `sysStat -> Header @19`, and the parameter pass published `global -> FileInfo @19` and `global -> Header @19` beside them. This is WORSE than the absent edge GO39 fixed: a consumer grouping by source sees the same fact twice, once unattributable, and cannot tell which to keep. REAL CORPUS FREQUENCY: 353 global-source rows on the go-stdlib subset alone, led by `src/archive/tar/common.go:617` — `var sysStat func(fi fs.FileInfo, h *Header, doNameLookups bool) error` — which is the same declaration shape as this fixture's subject, in the standard library itself. THE FIX IS SHAPE-PROVEN AND SCOPE-TESTED: a `var_spec`/`const_spec` reached in the walk answers its first non-blank identifier ONLY when it has no function/method/func_literal ancestor; otherwise it keeps walking so the enclosing function answers, because LocalsAreNotSymbols makes a function-local var/const not a graph node and attributing to it would trade a dangling source for an unresolvable one. THE FIVE FORBIDDEN ROWS ARE THE OTHER HALF, each a shape a cheaper fix gets wrong: (a) `global -> FileInfo` and (b) `global -> Header` are the defect itself — the duplicate unattributable edges that must not come back; (c) `global -> Header @19` pins that fixing the package-scope case must not ALSO move the blank `var _ func(*Header)` on line 30, whose `global` is honest because `_` names no graph node — a fix that returned the spec's name without the blank test would claim `_ -> Header`; (d) `localHook -> Header` is forbidden because a FUNCTION-LOCAL var is not a symbol, and a fix that returned the spec's name unconditionally would publish exactly this unresolvable source; (e) `inner -> Header` is forbidden for the same reason inside a package var's func literal, whose correct answer is the owning var `Registry`. NOT PINNED: `exports` rows (owned by the export pass, unchanged here) and confidence/tier, which are identical for any declared_type reference.

expectRelationships.comment: The subject: the func type's first parameter type attributes to the var that declares it.
The func type's second parameter type, same declaration.
CONTROL: a named non-func type was already correct before the fix and must stay correct.
CONTROL: two names, one type — each name is its own binding.
CONTROL: the second of the two-name declaration.
A blank name at package scope names no graph node, so `global` is the honest source and must STAY.
A function-local var attributes to the ENCLOSING FUNCTION, which is what the function_declaration branch answers.
A func literal owned by a package var keeps answering the owning var's name.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE DEFECT: the parameter pass's duplicate unattributable edge. The var_spec pass already publishes sysStat -> FileInfo; this one must not exist.
THE DEFECT, second parameter of the same declaration.
A function-local func type must NOT attribute to the local's name. LocalsAreNotSymbols makes it no graph node, so this source could never be resolved by a consumer.
Same for a local inside a package var's func literal; the correct answer there is the owning var Registry.
The blank identifier names no node. A fix that returned the spec's name without the blank test would move this row onto `_`, which resolves to nothing.
